new.tovw: Lead grade D: county history only, located by the 1872 plat
new.n: Bogus Corners, the counterfeiters' crossroads, Lyon Twp
new.pl: Corner of secs 2, 3, 10 and 11, T1N R7E, Lyon Twp, Oakland Co, on the Grand River plank road about 1 mi E of New Hudson
new.st: The 1877 county history says Samuel Barton, 'of bogus coin fame', settled at the place since known as Bogus Corners. His gang included Henry Eddy, who died of poison, and Peter Loomis, the blacksmith and principal workman, later sent to the penitentiary. In 1877 the land at the Corners belonged to Walter Bowers, George W. Button and Jonathan Taylor; on the 1872 plat their tracts meet at the sec 2/3/10/11 corner on the plank road.
new.t: Dies, bogus coin and slag are the targets; the corner is a road junction with private land on all sides. Access: private: permission.
src: Durant, History of Oakland County, Michigan (1877), p. 215
Atlas of Oakland County, Michigan (1872), Lyon Twp plate (Ancestry image 31617_072123-00894)
pinev: 1872 plat: Button 240 a. sec 3, G. W. Button 60 a. NW sec 11, Bowers 80 a. secs 2/10, Taylor 79 a. NE sec 10, meeting at the sec 2/3/10/11 corner; corner from BLM PLSS (sec 2 SW corner 42.5061, -83.5971); r300.

new.tovw: Lead grade D: county histories only, no period paper yet
new.n: Bliss's 'Travelers' Home', the Prairie Pirates' tavern at Inlet Grove
new.pl: Inlet Grove locality, Lee Co; the tavern is not placed inside the grove
new.st: The 1878 Ogle County history ('Prairie Pirates') names Adolphus Bliss, Corydon Dewey and Charles West as first settlers at Inlet Grove about 1835-36. Bliss's log tavern, the 'Travelers' Home', was 'a rendezvous for counterfeiters, or at least a distributing point for their currency and coin'. The 1877 Winnebago County history tells the same. Pin is the grove, not the tavern.
new.t: Tavern site not placed inside the grove; a Lee Co plat or the 1893 Lee Co 'Recollections' may name the quarter-section. Private farmland.
src: History of Ogle County, Illinois (1878), 'Prairie Pirates'
History of Winnebago County, Illinois (1877), p. 263

new.tovw: Lead grade D: one county-history line, no period paper yet
new.n: French Lake's buried money, sec 7 Jefferson Twp (1839)
new.pl: Sec 7 T1N R8E, Jefferson Twp, Green Co (1884 county history)
new.st: The 1884 Green County history, in the Jefferson and Juda chapter, says an early settler named French Lake buried his money on section 7 in 1839. Nothing more is told. Pin is the section centre, not the spot.
new.t: A one-line county-history note; an 1839 cabin site on a full section. Find the Lake entry on the GLO tract book and the 1873 Green Co plat. Private farmland.
src: History of Green County, Wisconsin (1884), p. 1050

set.tovw: Lead grade D: county-history retelling of a gallows confession; section-placed
set.pl: NW corner of sec 16 T76N R6W, Iowa Twp, Washington Co (Burrell 1909); the red oak is gone
pinev: Burrell 1909 names the section: 'the northwest corner of section 16 in Iowa'. Gallup lived in Clay Twp but the burial is placed in Iowa Twp. No period paper yet.

Burrell's 1844 township list gives Iowa as T76-77N R6W; Highland (T77N R6W) was split off in 1854, so Iowa Twp is T76N R6W. Sec 16 from BLM PLSS (box 41.2939-41.3083 / -91.5615 to -91.5424); pin just inside the NW corner. If the story predates 1854, sec 16 T77N R6W (now Highland) is the other reading.
set.t: Look for an old red oak or its stump near the NW corner of sec 16; this was the school section, sold in small lots. Private: permission needed.
